classification.classification_note: The fuzz harness accepts an attacker-controlled universal-WASM AOT custom section, the loader skips AST function-body loading, validation still accepts the empty expression, and the AOT compiler later reads the nonexistent top element of its internal value stack in `FunctionCompiler::stackPop()`.

bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is a 184-byte WebAssembly module whose bytes contain the custom-section name `wasmedge` and whose ordinary type section begins `01 05 01 60 00 01 7c`, i.e. one function type `() -> f64`. In vulnerable `lib/driver/fuzzTool.cpp`, `WasmEdge::Driver::FuzzTool` constructs `Configure Conf` but never calls `Conf.getRuntimeConfigure().setForceInterpreter(true)` before parsing the attacker bytes. `Loader::loadModule()` therefore pre-scans custom sections, recognizes the attacker-controlled `wasmedge` section, successfully loads its payload as `AST::AOTSection`, and marks the module `WASMType = UniversalWASM`. During the later ordinary code-section load, `loadSegment(AST::CodeSegment&)` sees `!ForceInterpreter && WASMType != InputType::WASM` and seeks past the function body instead of calling `loadExpression()`, so the code segment keeps its locals but its `Expr` is left empty. `FormChecker::checkExpr()` returns success immediately when `Instrs.size() == 0`, so module validation does not reject that empty-expression, non-void function. The fuzz harness then still calls `AOT::Compiler::compile(...)`, which pairs the skipped-body code segment with function type 0, compiles no instructions, and falls through to the synthetic end-of-function `compileReturn()`. Because the resolved LLVM return type is scalar `f64`, `compileReturn()` executes `stackPop()` and `Stack.back()` reads from an empty vector, matching the saved AddressSanitizer SEGV in `FunctionCompiler::stackPop()`. The fix closes this path by forcing interpreter mode in the fuzz harness before parsing, so the loader no longer treats attacker-controlled `wasmedge` sections as active AOT metadata and the real wasm function body is loaded into the AST instead of being skipped.

source.description: First non-harness parser step that consumes vulnerability-relevant attacker bytes. When the custom-section name is `wasmedge`, loader materializes embedded AOT metadata and flips module state to `UniversalWASM`.
source.value_from: Static inspection of the exact staged `poc` shows the ASCII string `wasmedge` in the witness bytes (`strings -a poc` and `xxd -g 1 -l 256 poc` both show it). On the crashing path this block succeeds, because the later code-segment load takes the `WASMType != InputType::WASM` body-skip branch.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `stackPop()` dereferences the AOT compiler's empty internal value stack with `Stack.back()`.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports a `SEGV on unknown address` caused by a `READ` at `lib/aot/compiler.cpp:4785:18` in `FunctionCompiler::stackPop`, called from `compileReturn()` line 3501 and `FunctionCompiler::compile()` line 679.

root_cause.description: The fuzz harness parses attacker input with the default runtime configuration, leaving `ForceInterpreter` false. That allows embedded `wasmedge` AOT sections to switch loader mode and suppress AST expression loading before the same module is sent to the AOT compiler.
root_cause.note: The fix adds `Conf.getRuntimeConfigure().setForceInterpreter(true);` between `Configure Conf;` and `Loader::Loader Loader(Conf);`, preventing the later AOT-only `!Conf.getRuntimeConfigure().isForceInterpreter()` branch from being taken on fuzz inputs.

tainted_value_origin.description: The exact witness's ordinary wasm type section contributes a non-void return type for function type 0. That attacker-derived return arity is the value later consumed by `compileReturn()` to decide it must pop one stack value.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The staged `poc` begins with ordinary type-section bytes `01 05 01 60 00 01 7c`, which encode one function type with zero parameters and one result byte `0x7c` (`F64`).

parser_admitted.description: The exact staged `poc` is accepted by `Loader.parseModule(...)` and materialized as an `AST::Module`; otherwise the later validation and AOT compilation steps would not execute.

coarse_trace.summary: The vulnerable fuzz harness leaves `ForceInterpreter` disabled, then parses attacker bytes whose custom section name `wasmedge` is accepted as active AOT metadata and flips the module into `UniversalWASM` mode.

The same witness still loads an ordinary wasm function type `() -> f64`, but the code-segment loader now skips `loadExpression()` and leaves the matching function body empty because `WASMType != InputType::WASM`.
Validation treats the empty code expression as success because `checkExpr()` returns immediately on zero instructions, so the non-void, skipped-body function survives `Validator::validate(*Module)`.
AOT compilation pairs the empty code segment with type 0, which still returns `f64`, compiles no instructions, and reaches the synthetic end-of-function return with an empty internal value stack.
Because the function type is non-void, `compileReturn()` executes `stackPop()`, and `Stack.back()` on the empty vector triggers the observed AddressSanitizer SEGV read.

fine_trace.note: Root cause. The fuzz harness constructs `Conf` with default `ForceInterpreter == false` and immediately parses attacker bytes under that config. The later fix inserts `Conf.getRuntimeConfigure().setForceInterpreter(true);` here, so the vulnerability-relevant missing obligation is to disable AOT-section handling for fuzz inputs before parsing.

Source. `loadModule()` reads custom-section names from the attacker-controlled wasm. The exact staged witness contains the name `wasmedge`, so on the crashing path this block copies the corresponding payload, parses it as `AST::AOTSection`, and sets `WASMType = InputType::UniversalWASM`.

The same witness still loads the ordinary wasm function signature. From the exact bytes `01 05 01 60 00 01 7c`, this step materializes a single return type `0x7c` (`F64`) for function type 0, so the eventual function is non-void.

Because step 1 left `ForceInterpreter` false and step 2 changed `WASMType` away from plain `WASM`, the code-segment loader takes the skip branch and seeks past the function body instead of calling `loadExpression()`. The code segment still exists, but `CodeSeg.getExpr().getInstrs()` is left empty on the crashing path.

Module validation passes the code segment's instruction view and expected return types into this helper. When step 4 leaves `Instrs.size() == 0`, `checkExpr()` returns success immediately and never checks that the non-void return type from step 3 has a produced value. That validation gap lets `FuzzTool` continue into AOT compilation.

AOT compilation pairs each code segment with the type index from the function section. For the exact witness there is one function and one code segment, so the skipped-body code segment is paired with type 0, whose return vector from step 3 is still `F64`.

The function compiler enters the function using the resolved non-void type from step 6, calls `compile(...)` on the empty instruction vector from step 4, and still falls through to `compileReturn()` unconditionally. Because no wasm instructions were compiled, no `stackPush()` populated the internal value stack.

The resolved LLVM return type is scalar `F64`, so `Ty.isVoidTy()` and `Ty.isStructTy()` are both false. `compileReturn()` therefore takes the scalar-return branch and demands one value from `stackPop()` even though step 7 left `Stack` empty.
Sink. `stackPop()` executes `Stack.back()` while `Stack` is still empty, so it reads past the vector's logical bounds and triggers the saved AddressSanitizer SEGV / wild-address read at line 4785.

format.name: WebAssembly module with embedded WasmEdge AOT custom section
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are only the exact staged `poc`: a 184-byte wasm module whose bytes include the custom-section name `wasmedge` and whose ordinary type section encodes one function type `() -> f64` (`01 05 01 60 00 01 7c`). Under vulnerable `lib/driver/fuzzTool.cpp`, `ForceInterpreter` remains false, so the loader accepts that `wasmedge` payload as active AOT metadata, later skips `loadExpression()` for the matching code segment, validator accepts the resulting empty `Expr`, and AOT compilation reaches `compileReturn()` with an empty value stack. Stage 01 preserved only this witness, so this contract does not generalize beyond inputs that reproduce the same host-accepted `wasmedge` AOT state, empty loaded expression, and non-void function type.

evidence_limitations: Stage 01 preserved only the vulnerable AddressSanitizer reproduction. Stage 02 did not execute a fixed build or a second detector, so `patch_resolves: true` is source-grounded from `patch.diff` rather than dynamic differential validation.

run_flags.json sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 used only the staged source, patch, sanitizer trace, reproduction report, and static inspection of the exact witness bytes; no targeted instrumentation was performed.
